stories.title: Deaths of woman and man treated as murder-suicide
stories.summary: Gardaí are treating the death of a Brazilian woman in Limerick as a murder-suicide after the body of her husband, who is suspected of her killing, was found in Cork at the weekend. Jady Cristine Pereira Rosa, a law graduate from Brazil, was found dead at an apartment on Lower Cecil Street on Friday morning. It is understood that friends of Ms Pereira Rosa, who had been waiting outside the building for her, contacted gardaí when she did not appear. When gardaí arrived at the scene they discovered her body in an apartment upstairs.

stories.title: New EU-wide product repair rules come into force
stories.summary: New EU rules have come into force designed to encourage consumers to repair rather than replace products to tackle the estimated 35 million tonnes of waste the premature disposal of consumer goods generates across the bloc. The 'right to repair' regulations introduce new rights and supports aimed at encouraging repair over disposal, including a repair obligation for manufacturers of certain products and the establishment of a national repair platform to help consumers locate repair services. The rules apply to household and electronic products such as washing machines, vacuum cleaners, mobile phones, and tablets. The regulations are designed to make it easier for consumers to access repair services when products develop faults after the seller's guarantee period.

stories.title: Planned increases in excise duty will not go ahead - Govt
stories.summary: The Government is taking a step-by-step approach to fuel subsidies, Minister for Agriculture Martin Heydon has said, following confirmation that the planned reversal of excise duty fuel cuts in September and October will not go ahead. Earlier, a government spokesperson said that the first two stages of the phased re-introduction of full excise duty fuel costs between 1 September and the start of December will be delayed. In order to do so, the Dáil will be recalled for one day, next Friday, to agree to a financial resolution confirming the matter. He said that the Government is aware of "the impact that the reinstatement of those levies would have had on consumers", but denied that the decision was taken to stave off potential protests.

stories.title: Shein shrinks value to $27 billion, at best, in IPO
stories.summary: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein's valuation has dropped by around 70% from its private market peak four years ago, as it aims to raise up to HK$13.86 billion ($1.77 billion) in its Hong Kong IPO launched today. The long-awaited Hong Kong IPO comes after Shein scrapped plans to list in New York and London over the past four years. It is selling 280 million shares between HK$47.60 and HK$49.50 per share, the filings showed, valuing it at close to $27 billion at the top of that range. Reuters last week exclusively reported the Shein IPO was set to value the company at around a quarter of the $100 billion it was worth in 2022.

stories.title: Wartime elections would 'split' Ukraine, warns Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has cautioned that wartime elections would currently be too dangerous for Ukraine, after a call by his former defence minister to organise a vote. "I believe that in a war like this, elections as such are a huge risk. Elections right now are a tsunami for the country that will split Ukraine," Mr Zelensky said in remarks made public today. On Wednesday, ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for wartime elections, arguing that Ukraine faced a crisis of governance, in the biggest internal challenge to Mr Zelensky since Russia's invasion in 2022. "Democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia," Mr Fedorov said in a video address posted on YouTube.

stories.title: McCartan: Newbies brought 'freshness' to Cork panel
stories.summary: After being in the last six All-Ireland camogie finals and winning three of those, it may have been difficult to change a winning formula. Getting to so many successive finals prove that Cork camogie has clearly been in a golden age. But this season saw a lot of change in the Cork camp. After a very difficult start, forward Sorcha McCartan credited a "freshness" that the new players brought into the senior camogie set up during the season just gone. "I think they brought a bit of a freshness in terms of maybe there was less of a tense atmosphere. Not that the girls that left were tense, but I suppose they were around for so long that they brought a bit of seriousness to it. "They understood the magnitude of trouble that we were in. We had one win on the board at the end of May. That's really unheard of for a Cork camogie team.

stories.title: Iraola: Liverpool didn't deserve to lose v Newcastle
stories.summary: New Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has said that his side didn't deserve to lose against Newcastle United after Dominik Szoboszlai rescued a late point for the Reds at St James' Park. Newcastle led 1-0 and 2-1, but Liverpool clawed their way back twice, finally securing a point with Szoboszlai's spot-kick in the ninth minute of stoppage time. It was an underwhelming display against a Newcastle side that let itself down with a couple of costly defensive lapses. "It's not the result you wanted before the game, but obviously finishing, scoring in the last minute, it gives you a better taste," Iraola said. "I don't think we deserve to lose the game today.

stories.title: Munster beat Connacht to extend winning streak to seven
stories.summary: An already-qualified Munster will move on to the Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship final in unbeaten form following a 47-12 win away to Connacht. Although Leinster's earlier victory over Ulster ended Connacht's hopes of reaching next week's final at Dexcom Stadium, they put in a gutsy display in their first game in front of the fully-completed Clan Stand. Uillin Eilian had a dream start to her Connacht senior debut, grabbing a third-minute try, but Munster gradually took control of the scoreboard to lead 21-5 at half-time. Alana McInerney's intercept effort was followed by Alisha Flynn driving in under the posts, and then Caitríona Finn's slick 33rd-minute score brought her tally to 11 points.

stories.title: The wild true tale of the syndicate that tried to beat the lotto
stories.summary: What I love about this story is how it illuminates a pivotal moment in Ireland's history in a fascinating and highly entertaining way. Beat The Lotto is a heist film, a caper, a thriller that builds to a very specific climax. In the end, do they win the jackpot or not!? But it’s also about the Irish psyche—how we felt, and still feel, about institutions and taking on the system. Listen: The team behind Beat The Lotto talk to Miriam O'Callaghan The idea for Beat The Lotto first sparked over a decade ago at a friend’s wedding. I found myself sitting beside a guy who worked in big data, which felt relatively new at the time. I asked him if there were any interesting stories in the data world that might make a good documentary. He laughed and said, "No, no! But a story you should look at is that time a syndicate tried to buy all the numbers in the lottery!" Suddenly, I was transported back to 1992. I’d always loved that story. I remembered listening to the radio before school, hearing about a syndicate attempting to buy every possible lottery combination. The sense of intrigue was palpable—a race against time as the lottery scrambled to slow them down.

stories.title: Hosepipe ban extension for 13 counties
stories.summary: The nationwide hosepipe ban in place since late last month has been extended in 13 counties, with the ban lifting on 26 August for 13 other counties, Uisce Éireann has said. The Water Conservation Order came into effect as Ireland's prolonged spell of hot, dry weather put drinking water supplies under pressure. The order applies to all households and prohibits the use of hosepipes for activities such as washing cars, watering gardens and filling paddling pools. Uisce Éireann extended the ban until the end of September for Carlow, Cork, Dublin, Kildare, Kilkenny, Laois, Limerick, Meath, Offaly, Tipperary, Waterford, Wexford and Wicklow, saying that the supplies need more time to recover.

stories.title: Rise in farm payment schemes to tackle fodder shortages
stories.summary: Payments given to farmers under a number of schemes will see an increase from 70% to 75% as part of a plan to alleviate the effects of fodder shortages. The Department of Agriculture has said both the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) and Complementary Redistributive Income Support for Sustainability scheme (CRISS) will see the increase, as well as the Eco Scheme. Minister for Agriculture Martin Heydon said that rules around the Agri-Climate Rural Environment Scheme (ACRES) will also see more flexibility and will now allow for the mowing of almost 26,000 hectares of land from now, rather than from 31 August. "My department administers €1.6 billion worth of payments over the course of the next four months that farmers expect at a certain set time for the different activities that they're carrying out. And I can't do anything to undermine the scheduling of them or to delay in any way those payments," he said.

stories.title: Iran dismisses threat of new US sanctions as desperation
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister dismissed the threat of new US sanctions as a sign of desperation and said the expected new measures would fail to defeat Tehran. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is due to hold a press conference at 2pm EDT (7pm Irish time) tomorrow, has threatened to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran. Iran's economy is already under huge pressure from international sanctions, its infrastructure has been hit repeatedly and thousands of people have been killed in airstrikes on the Islamic Republic since the US and Israel launched attacks on 28 February. But Tehran remains defiant after nearly six months of war and has brought shipping to a virtual standstill in the Strait of Hormuz, refusing to allow unauthorised oil tankers to transit a waterway that is vital for global oil shipments.

stories.title: Feely already dreaming of scaling senior heights in 2027
stories.summary: While the achievements of this year are still very fresh in her mind, Roscommon's Aisling Feely is eagerly anticipating the prospect of playing senior championship football in 2027. Courtesy of their emphatic 2-12 to 0-06 triumph over Fermanagh in the TG4 All-Ireland intermediate football championship decider at Croke Park on 2 August, the Rossies will be one of 12 counties to feature in the top-tier of the LGFA next summer. Even before taking part in the race for the Brendan Martin Cup, the primrose and blue will lock horns with newly-crowned All-Ireland senior winners Galway and Mayo in next year’s Connacht championship at the highest grade of ladies football. This will help to make it a three-team series out in the west once again, as it was when the previous season’s All-Ireland intermediate champions Leitrim made the brief step up to senior football in 2025, and Feely is excited about this new opportunity for Roscommon. "We saw Leitrim do it two years ago. We would have been always there or thereabouts with them. They knocked us out in the quarter-final that year by two points and they went on to win it. That gave us a bit of inspiration. If Leitrim can do it, why can’t we. We’re just as good. To get up to senior is absolutely massive," Feely acknowledged.

stories.title: All Blacks worthy winners as they outscore Springboks
stories.summary: New Zealand overcame a tough physical challenge to outscore South Africa five tries to one and win the first test 33-16 at Ellis Park on Saturday to go one-up in the four-match series. The All Blacks had been underdogs going into the first international of their eight-match tour but took full advantage of the hosts' numerous handling errors and ill discipline for a statement victory that ended a 12-match winning streak for the Springboks and will rock the confidence of the world champions. Will Jordan extended his run as New Zealand's record try scorer with two tries that bookended scores from Josh Moorby, Fabian Holland and Luke Jacobson. Ruben Love kicked over four conversions. South Africa’s try came from Andre Esterhuizen with three penalties and a conversion from Cheslin Kolbe.

stories.title: How to get out of your comfort zone and fight indecision
stories.summary: As summer draws to a close, I can't help but think about all the things I said I'd like to do this year but haven't yet. From getting my steps in and reading more, to journaling every night, cutting down on screen time and even setting up a TikTok page, my list is getting longer by the day. The funny thing is, I have made little steps towards some of them. I bought the notebook to write in, I’ve got a page of content ideas sitting in my Notes app, I’ve got a pile of unread books on my windowsill, and I even have the usual screen time reminders set on my phone. Yet somehow, I still haven't quite committed to actually jumping into anything. Sure, I've prepped and planned, but when it comes to taking that final step and turning those intentions into habits, I seem to keep finding a reason to put it off.

stories.title: Bryant concerned that Troubles Bill is 'misunderstood'
stories.summary: The UK's Northern Ireland Secretary has said that he has concerns that some people have "misunderstood" parts of the Northern Ireland Troubles Bill, adding that it is about "getting answers for families". Speaking during a visit to Dublin, Chris Bryant stated that the relationship between the British and Irish governments was essential when it comes to progressing the Troubles Bill. The bill would repeal and replace the controversial Legacy Act introduced by the previous Conservative government, ending the immunity scheme brought in under the law that was ruled unlawful in the courts. The British Labour Party’s bill, agreed as part of a joint framework with the Irish Government, will put in place a reformed Legacy Commission with enhanced powers.

stories.title: TikTok could face Europe-wide ban, Irish MEP warns

The company has declined to appear before the Oireachtas Media committee to address the posting of videos on the platform of people driving down motorways the wrong way in the wake of last week's collision on the M9 motorway. Five teenagers died when the car in which they were travelling the wrong way down the M9 motorway collided head-on with another vehicle, seriously injuring three women and a boy in the same family.

stories.title: Moody's lifts Ireland's sovereign rating to 'Aa2'
stories.summary: The National Treasury Management Agency has welcomed credit ratings agency Moody's upgrade of Ireland's long-term sovereign credit rating. This marks the first upgrade of Ireland's rating from Moody's since April 2023 and is the first time that Moody's has rated Ireland at Aa2 since 2010. Moody's on Friday upgraded Ireland's sovereign credit rating to "Aa2" from "Aa3" and reiterated its positive outlook, saying it expects improvements in the country's economic and fiscal strength to continue. The ratings agency said its assessment was supported by Ireland's strong institutional framework, effective policymaking and resilience to recent changes in US trade and tax policies.

stories.title: McIlroy takes heart from BMW Championship fightback
stories.summary: Rory McIlroy admits there is much room for improvement in his game, but took solace from his spirited display in the final round of the BMW Championship. Wyndham Clark prevailed at Bellerive Country Club, but was pushed by a resurgent McIlroy who was joint-leader with three holes to play before eventually finishing third. Clark had entered the final round with a five-shot buffer, but three bogeys over the first 10 holes brought the chasers into play. His playing partner McIlroy drew level and remained tied for the lead with three holes but the world number two had to settle for third, four strokes back, as Clark finished with three consecutive birdies to claim a three-shot victory and third PGA Tour win of the season.

stories.title: Kobe-mania and the Irish experiment
stories.summary: The AFL's Irish experiment nearly failed before even it really even began - and it all came down to a split-second decision in the 1987 Victorian Football League preliminary final between Melbourne and Hawthorn. The VFL was three years from morphing into the AFL and a huge crowd had gathered to watch what turned into a manic final quarter with tennis legend Pat Cash even interrupting a family holiday to attend. Melbourne missed chance after chance to kill off the Hawks’ challenge in the final minutes of the match, Simon Eishold’s incredible mis-hit hook behind long remembered by Demons fans, but it was the final play that saw it go down in infamy and left recently-recruited Dubliner Jim Stynes labelled as a laughing stock. Kept alive by Melbourne’s inefficiency, Gary Buckenara was given one last chance to win it from Hawthorn but from way out, it was a low percentage chance.
